title: Trace annotation templates and dashboard iteration notes
content:
Objective:
A compact set of trace-annotation templates and an iteration checklist to speed dashboard changes for inference rollouts. Focus: short, operator-friendly annotations that power drilldowns (model, route, tenant, kv-warmth, batch-size).

Context / motivation:
- We keep rebuilding dashboards for each rollout because trace metadata is inconsistent across services.
- Operators need 1-click jumps from a slow-quantile panel to a focused trace view with tenant + model version pre-applied.
- Keep trace size and cardinality bounded while preserving high-value keys.

Guiding constraints (opinionated):
1) Max 8 annotation keys per request (fewer on high-throughput fanout).
2) Prefer short keys (<= 16 chars) and canonical values (no free-text where possible).
3) Annotate at request entry, and emit final state before response completes to capture fallback/multi-model decisions.
4) Make boolean flags explicit (true/false) rather than omitting.

Core annotation template (recommended order, prioritizes operator drilldown):
- s_tid: session id (64-char hex or uuid)
- tenant_id: tenant short id (alphanumeric)
- model_ver: model-id@semantic-version (e.g., llama2-13b@v2.1)
- route: API route name (e.g., /v1/chat/completions)
- kv_hit: enum {cold,warm,hit,evicted} (see kv-encoding section)
- batch_sz: integer (requests in batch)
- quant_profile: short tag (none, q4_0, q8_0, int8-lite)
- fallback: enum {none,smaller-model,queued,region-fallback} 

Optional enrichment keys (emit only when present to avoid cardinality explosion):
- eval_id: seeded prompt set id (for rollout comparisons)
- latency_stage_ms: comma-separated stage latencies (e.g., compile:5,kvcache:2,decode:18)
- prompt_hash: 8-char hash for grouping repeated prompts

KV-encoding convention (critical for warm/cold analysis):
- kv_hit values map to operator-friendly states: cold (first request, high disk load), warm (cache warmed this session), hit (cache returned), evicted (cache miss due to eviction).
- Emit a separate kv_probe boolean for synthetic probes to avoid polluting production cardinality.

Sampling and retention notes:
- Adaptive sampling: full traces for 1 in 100 requests; 1 in 10 for tail quantile (>=95th ms) via server-side sampling hook.
- Always keep 100% of traces tagged with eval_id or fallback != none for 30d.
- Redact PII at ingestion and mark redaction via annotation redacted:true.

Dashboard iteration checklist (pre-deploy -> post-rollout):
- Pre-deploy:
  - Confirm model_ver annotation standardized across serving agents (ENG-1423).
  - Add trace links on 95/99 panels that pre-fill tenant_id + model_ver filters.
  - Add a compact 'trace-hit-rate' panel: percent of requests where kv_hit==hit by tenant cohort.
  - Create a synthetic probe with kv_probe=true to validate cold-vs-warm curves in staging.

- During canary:
  - Enable enhanced trace sampling for canary tenant slice (eval_id set).
  - Monitor fallback counts and create a live alert when fallback != none exceeds threshold for 5m.
  - Inspect prompt_hash clusters for prompt-specific latency regressions.

- Post-rollout (1–3 days):
  - Run a dashboard audit: remove any low-value high-cardinality enrichment keys.
  - Move stable signals to 30d aggregates and reduce trace sampling to baseline.
  - Run a short retro and add a concrete metric to metric-contracts if useful (e.g., model_switch_rate).

Operator quickcards (copy these to the runbook):
- Jump to tail traces: click 99th latency panel -> traces -> auto-filter tenant_id + model_ver.
- If kv_hit shows 'evicted' spikes: check eviction_rate, eviction_cause tag, and scaling events.
- If fallback increases: check model variant capacity, routing policy logs, region availability.

Common pitfalls (from previous rollouts):
- Using free-text model names (eg 'Llama 2 big') created thousands of variants; enforce model naming in model onboarding.
- Emitting long arrays in latency_stage_ms caused dashboard parser timeouts; use comma-separated short keys instead.
- Leaving eval_id optional meant we lost direct linkage between rollout and trace set in 2 incidents — make eval_id required for canaries.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we want to standardize quant_profile taxonomy across Dedicated/private (cloud partners require mapping)? (decision: design sync with infra + partnerships team)
- Should prompt_hash be computed client-side (SDK) to reduce server CPU? tradeoffs: SDK adoption vs centralization.

Next steps (owners):
- Maya: draft RFC for trace key canonicalization and push to eng-all by 2026-03-05.
- Priya: add trace pre-fill links to dashboard skeleton and create PR (obs-dashboards repo).
- Diego: prototype adaptive sampler that pins eval_id traces for 30d and emits sampling metadata.

Notes to self / quick references:
- Slack thread: #ops-observability "kv-warmth-probes" (link pinned)
- Jira: ENG-1423 (model naming enforcement), ENG-1588 (trace sampling prototyping)
- GitHub snippet: see PR 88 for trace enrichment library changes

——
Rough timeline: 2 sprint rollout: sprint 1 (templates + dashboard skeleton + synthetic probes), sprint 2 (canary sampling + alerts + retro).

If anything needs to be trimmed for cardinality I will annotate the exact key to drop (keep list trim-safe).

End of notes.
